name: İzmir
summary_text: Model estimate (route 3, best-knowledge delta): İzmir — the most secular city in the country, visible community despite the national crackdown; the 13th Pride Week and its events were banned, and in May–June 2025 police broke up Pride-related public events with batons, tear gas, water cannons and rubber bullets. Mülteci-Der's report on Syrian trans women living here found they cannot find work, face exploitation and harassment when they do, and have 'no faith in justice'. National frame: the leaked October 2025 draft would criminalise 'conduct contrary to biological sex' and its promotion (up to 3 years) and restrict gender-affirming care (minimum age 25); a 2025 rights report records hostility as explicit state policy, six violations of the right to life, trans people most affected. Scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Turkey.

sources.title: Türkiye: Draft Law Threatens LGBT People with Prison | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (29 Oct 2025): a leaked '11th Judicial Package' would amend the penal and civil codes with articles threatening LGBT people — behaviour 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' and its 'promotion' (up to three years' prison, amending the indecent-acts provision); sharp restrictions on gender-affirming care (minimum age 25, onerous eligibility); potential charges against trans people, care providers, civil-society organisations and journalists; justified as protecting 'the family and public morals'.

Kaos GL's LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025, 'The Year of the Family: A Major Siege Against LGBTI+ People': hostility institutionalised as explicit state policy — presidency-centred targeting, the family ministry as implementing body, religious-broadcast regulator and content restrictions on expression and artistic freedom, one LGBTI+ organisation closed, digital-platform penalties and broadcast censorship; six violations of the right to life documented (three recorded as hate-motivated), trans people the most affected; no state hate-crime statistics exist so data rests on media reporting. Launched at a public event in the capital.
